sources.title: Interview note containing the one-pass linked-list subrange reversal question
Deterministic Java validation against an array subrange-reversal oracle
Source-first isolated review for the reverse-between candidate

claims.text: The recovered source asks for a one-pass reversal of linked-list nodes from m through n, but does not preserve indexing convention, invalid-range behavior, null-input behavior or whether mutation is required.

Keeping before immediately ahead of the reversed region and current at that region's tail lets each current.next node be detached and inserted at the front while preserving connectivity until the whole interval is reversed.

The implementation performs one forward positioning/traversal path without restarting from the head and stores only a dummy node plus a constant number of references, yielding linear time and O(1) auxiliary space.

The exact Java implementation passes seven fixed interval cases and 5000 deterministic randomized valid linked-list/range combinations against an array-reversal oracle while checking result length and absence of extra nodes or cycles.

validation.reported_stdout: PASS fixed=7 randomized=5000 oracle=array-subrange-reversal ordered=true acyclic=true
checks: middle, prefix, suffix and full-list reversal
m == n no-op and single-element list
5000 deterministic randomized valid ranges against an array-subrange-reversal oracle
result length preservation and no extra node or cycle

boundary_tests.expected: dummy predecessor permits the same pointer-rewiring loop without a head-specific branch
tail remains null and the suffix boundary stays connected
returns the original ordering without pointer movement
null and m < 1 fail fast; n beyond length remains outside the declared candidate contract

findings: The candidate is source-bounded and clearly separates recovered requirements from selected API assumptions.
The pointer invariant and one-forward-traversal explanation match the Java implementation.
The independent oracle exercises both fixed edge positions and 5000 deterministic randomized valid ranges without reusing the linked-list algorithm.
The tests guard against result truncation, extra nodes and cycles in addition to value-order correctness.
No unsupported project, online-judge or hidden-constraint claims were introduced.
Formal promotion remains blocked only by the pilot human-approval gate.
